tagline.text: A sunrise and sea-of-clouds ridge above Impalutao, Bukidnon, and a trek beginners can handle

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Impalutao, Impasug-ong, Bukidnon (trek starts at the Ant Farm basecamp)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: December–May (sea of clouds December–February, driest March–May)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Day trip (2–4 hours round trip) or overnight

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱900–1,800 (per person, day hike from Cagayan de Oro)

children.text: Panimahawa Ridge is a ridge trek in Barangay Impalutao, Impasug-ong, Bukidnon. The summit, reached in 2 to 4 hours round trip, rewards hikers with sunrise and a sea of clouds spilling over ridges and valleys, which makes it popular with first-time trekkers.

Panimahawa Ridge lies in Barangay Impalutao in the municipality of Impasug-ong, Bukidnon, in northern Mindanao. It is a mountain village reached by following the national highway from Cagayan de Oro toward Malaybalay, and the ridge area is described as part of the ancestral domain of the Higaonon people. The spelling varies from source to source, and you may also see it written as Paminahawa.
The biggest reason for its popularity is how easy it is to reach. From the Ant Farm basecamp, the starting point, the summit usually takes
1.5–2 hours
, and even with the descent the whole trip is over in
2–4 hours
. Round-trip distance is given as

depending on the source, and the path is an ordinary trail with no rope or rock-climbing sections. Even so, the short route packs in variety: you pass corn and pineapple fields, cross a river, and face a steep final climb, so it never gets dull. The summit elevation is given as
about 820–870 m
, and sources differ.

From the top you see ridges stacked one behind another and a view opening toward the Tagoloan canyon. If you climb at dawn, you may catch clouds filling the spaces between the ridges as the sun rises, and on clear days the high peaks of Bukidnon line up in the distance. Impalutao also has other ridges, such as Kapayawan, Gupalon, Kaanibungan and Ginahawan, so it is fun to compare their shapes from the summit.
You must hike with a local guide. You register at the Ant Farm basecamp and are assigned a guide, and hiking without one is not allowed. The registration and guide fees combined come to about

per person, which is easy on the budget. There is also a local custom of leaving coins at points along the trail, so the hike offers a taste of local culture as well as scenery. You can go up before dawn from Cagayan de Oro by changing between a bus and a motorcycle taxi and come back the same day, or you can pitch a tent on the summit and stay overnight. For visitors from Korea, the easiest plan is to base yourself in Cagayan de Oro (Laguindingan Airport) and pair a day hike with a nearby waterfall. Transport, itineraries, costs and cautions are laid out below, so read them before you set out.

blocks.title: Sunrise and sea of clouds at the summit

children.text: The standard approach on this ridge is to leave before dawn so you reach the summit before sunrise. Sources say that from December to February clouds often settle between the ridges. Weather depends on the morning's luck, so it helps to leave a couple of days of slack.

blocks.title: Neighboring ridges and the Tagoloan canyon

children.text: From the summit, neighboring ridges such as Kapayawan, Gupalon, Kaanibungan and Ginahawan stack up one behind another, and you look down into the canyon where the Tagoloan River flows. On clear days, high peaks of Bukidnon such as Mt. Dulang-dulang, Mt. Kitanglad and Mt. Kalatungan are said to be visible in the distance. When taking photos, try to include the ridges opposite the sunrise as well.

Right after the start you walk between corn and pineapple fields tended by villagers. It is a slow stroll through countryside scenery, a good way to warm up. Do not step into the fields and keep to the path.

blocks.title: The bamboo bridge and the Dila River crossing

children.text: After dropping into the canyon, you cross the river on a bamboo bridge. The bridge sways, so it is safer to cross one person at a time. After heavy rain the river can rise, and hikes may be restricted.
One source calls the final steep climb Deadman's Slope and describes it as about
long with a 30 to 45 degree gradient. It is short but breathtaking, so shorten your stride and go up slowly. After rain the red soil turns slippery, so take extra care on the way down.
Sources describe a custom of leaving coins at about two points on the trail and asking for safe passage. One source advises bringing small change of about
. It is local culture, so listen to your guide first and follow along respectfully.

You can pitch a tent on the flat ground near the summit and stay overnight. Some sources say there is no separate camping fee and you pay only the registration fee. There is almost no shade or windbreak and it gets very cold before dawn, so bring warm gear.
Near Impalutao is the Cedar (CEDAR) waterfall area, and many itineraries pair it with a post-hike swim. One blogger wrote that Gantungan Falls and Natigbasan Falls are about
apart. Check entrance fees and how to get there locally.

items.title: Day hike for sunrise
items.subtitle: Start before dawn, descend by morning and return to Cagayan de Oro

children.text: At the Agora Terminal in Cagayan de Oro, board a bus bound for Malaybalay or Davao that leaves early in the morning. Tell the conductor in advance that you want to get off at Impalutao Elementary School. Check departure times locally.
From Impalutao Elementary School, take a motorcycle taxi to the Ant Farm basecamp. Register, attend the safety briefing and meet your assigned guide.
Walk down through the cornfield section, cross the river on the bamboo bridge, then climb and refill your water at the stretch with a store.
Climb the last ridge ascent and reach the summit. To catch sunrise you need to start earlier. Enjoy the ridge and canyon views and have a snack.
Head back down the same trail to the basecamp. Change between a motorcycle taxi and a bus to return to Cagayan de Oro.
For an earlier sunrise, you can book a room in Impalutao or Impasug-ong town the night before and start around 4 a.m.

items.title: Overnight camping
items.subtitle: Climb in the afternoon to see both sunset and sunrise

children.text: Leave Cagayan de Oro and get off at Impalutao Elementary School. Have lunch before leaving or in the village.
Take a motorcycle taxi to the basecamp, register and set off with your guide. You can carry the camping gear yourself or hire a porter separately.
Arrive near the summit and pitch your tent away from cattle and their droppings. Have dinner while watching the sun go down behind the ridges.
Wake up at dawn for sunrise and the sea of clouds. Pack up after the sun is up.
Pack out all your trash, descend and head to Cagayan de Oro.
The summit has no shade or windbreak, so a waterproof tent and warm gear are necessary. A headlamp is a must.
There are direct flights from Manila (NAIA) to Laguindingan Airport (CGY) in Cagayan de Oro. The flight takes about
1.5 hours
Schedules and fares differ by airline, so check the latest information before you travel.

items.title: From the airport to Cagayan de Oro's Agora Terminal

children.text: From Laguindingan Airport, a shuttle, van or taxi to the Agora Terminal is reported to cost about
and take about
45–60 minutes
Rather than going straight from the airport to the terminal, staying a night in the city and catching an early bus is also a safe option.
From the Agora Terminal, take a bus bound for Malaybalay or Davao and get off at Impalutao Elementary School. The fare is reported at about
and the ride at about
3–4 hours
Before boarding, tell the conductor that you are getting off at Impalutao Elementary School.
From the airport, the whole journey is reported to take about 4 to 5 hours.

items.title: From the elementary school to the basecamp

children.text: A motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) from Impalutao Elementary School to the Ant Farm basecamp takes about
10–15 minutes
. Sources quote anywhere from ₱50 to ₱200 per person one way, so confirm before you get on.
The last stretch is an unpaved road that gets worse when it rains. If you are driving yourself, a high-clearance vehicle is safer.

Panimahawa Ridge is open all year, but for the sea of clouds and sunrise December to February is the most recommended. March to May is described as drier, with firmer soil that is easier to walk on. Even so, March to May is hot and dry by day with strong afternoon sun, so start early.

From June to November it is the rainy season, the red clay trail is slippery, and the Dila River can rise and restrict entry. One blog lists September to December as the rainy season, so sources differ; check the latest weather and notices before you go. Weekdays are relatively quiet, and weekends and holidays are said to require advance booking.

If you are not camping on the summit, staying in Cagayan de Oro is the easiest option. Because you need to catch an early bus, a room near the Agora Terminal makes getting around simpler. You can also find lodging in Impasug-ong or Malaybalay, so choose to suit your schedule.

There are almost no restaurants in Impalutao, the starting point. Bring a packed meal, water and snacks. There are stores along the trail, but prices are high and stock can run out, so do not count on them. After the hike you can eat in Impasug-ong or Malaybalay.
A guide is required. Weekends and holidays are said to require advance booking, so text the Ant Farm contact ahead of time. Contact numbers change over time, so check the latest announcement.
A start time of 3 to 4 a.m. is best. Afternoon showers are said to be frequent after sunrise.
Carry
1.5–2 liters
of water from the start. There is no water at the summit.
Wear shoes with good traction. Sandals and flat-soled shoes are slippery on the red clay trail.
Bring coins in small change. They are used for the coin custom.
Pack a headlamp, power bank, dry bag and a warm jacket. The summit can be cold at dawn.
Signal is weak or drops out in places. Save your map and schedule in advance.
Bring plenty of cash. There is said to be no ATM in Impalutao.
After heavy rain the Dila River can rise and cancel hikes, and the red clay trail becomes very slippery. Do not push on, and follow your guide's judgment.
You cannot enter the trail without a guide. You sign a logbook and a safety waiver.
The area near the summit is grazing land, so there are many cow droppings. Pitch your tent away from the cattle.
There are no trash bins. Carry all your trash down with you.
The bamboo bridge sways. Cross one person at a time and secure your pack.
The nearest medical facility is said to be the Impasug-ong health unit. In an emergency, ask through your guide.
Respect local culture such as the coin custom, and refrain from taking photos where your guide asks you not to.
This is the base city with the airport and the Agora Terminal. It takes about
3–4 hours
by bus to Impalutao.
The capital of Bukidnon, it lies on the national highway running south from Impalutao. It is a good place for lodging and meals.
A highland resort area near Impasug-ong that pairs well with a post-hike rest day. Check locally how to get there.
A waterfall area near Impalutao that many visitors combine with a swim after the hike. Check entrance fees and directions locally.
